units.summary: The company was founded in 2009.
units.quote: We are a third-party logistics company, founded in 2009.

units.summary: Kaisa Lindholm took over the company from her parents in 2021.
units.quote: I took over from my parents in 2021.

units.summary: The company was founded in 2009 by the Lindholm family.
units.quote: Third-party logistics (3PL) company founded in 2009 by the Lindholm family.

units.summary: The company has been under second-generation management since 2021, when Kaisa Lindholm took over as CEO.
units.quote: Second-generation management since 2021 (Kaisa Lindholm took over as CEO).

units.summary: Lumivaara is a Finnish family-owned logistics company.
units.quote: Lumivaara Logistics Oy is a Finnish family-owned third-party logistics (3PL) company headquartered in Vantaa.

units.summary: The company has around 130 people, in addition to agency staff during peak season.
units.quote: we are around 130 people, plus agency staff in the peak season.

units.summary: The company has about 130 employees, with temporary agency staff in peak seasons in addition.
units.quote: About 130 employees in total; on top of that, temporary agency staff in peak seasons

units.summary: The company had 134 employees measured as full-time equivalents at the end of 2025.
units.quote: The company employs 134 people (full-time equivalents at the end of 2025), complemented by temporary agency staff during peak seasons.

units.summary: Revenue in 2025 was about EUR 24.6 million.
units.quote: Revenue last year was about 24.6 million euros

units.summary: Revenue in 2025 was approximately EUR 24.6 million.
units.quote: Revenue 2025 approx. EUR 24.6 million

units.summary: Revenue in 2025 was EUR 24.6 million.
units.quote: Revenue in 2025 was EUR 24.6 million.

units.summary: The company operates three warehouses in Vantaa, Tampere and Oulu.
units.quote: We have three warehouses, Vantaa, Tampere, and Oulu.

units.summary: The company operates three warehouses: Vantaa, Tampere and Oulu.
units.quote: Three warehouses: Vantaa (main site and head office), Tampere and Oulu.

units.summary: The company operates warehouses in Vantaa, Tampere and Oulu.
units.quote: Operations are run from three warehouses in Vantaa, Tampere and Oulu

units.summary: The company provides contract warehousing, domestic road freight, e-commerce fulfillment, customs clearance and value-added services including labeling and kitting.
units.quote: We do contract warehousing, domestic road freight, e-commerce fulfillment, customs clearance, and some value-added services like labeling and kitting.

units.summary: Services include contract warehousing, domestic road freight, e-commerce fulfilment, customs clearance and value-added logistics services.
units.quote: Services: contract warehousing, domestic road freight, e-commerce fulfilment, customs clearance for customers importing from outside the EU, and value-added services (labelling, kitting, returns handling).

units.summary: The company provides contract warehousing, domestic road freight, e-commerce fulfilment, customs clearance and value-added logistics services.
units.quote: The company provides contract warehousing, domestic road freight, e-commerce fulfilment, customs clearance and value-added logistics services to business customers across Finland.

units.summary: The company has about 210 active business customers.
units.quote: Our customers are business customers, about 210 active ones.

units.summary: The company has around 210 active B2B customers.
units.quote: Around 210 active B2B customers.

units.summary: Retail and e-commerce is the largest segment, followed by industrial spare parts, chilled food and beverage, and a growing pharma and healthcare segment.
units.quote: Retail and e-commerce is the biggest segment, then industrial spare parts, chilled food, and beverage, and a growing pharma and healthcare segment.

units.summary: The largest customer segments are retail and e-commerce, industrial spare parts, chilled food and beverage, and pharma/healthcare.
units.quote: Largest segments: retail and e-commerce, industrial spare parts, chilled food and beverage, and a small but growing pharma/healthcare segment (GDP-certified area in Vantaa since 2024).

units.summary: The pharma and healthcare segment was the fastest-growing segment in 2025 and had the highest margin.
units.quote: The pharma and healthcare segment is the fastest-growing (+31 % in 2025) and has the highest margin.

units.summary: The company faces narrowing margins, rising wages and fuel costs, and downward price pressure from large retail customers.
units.quote: our margins are getting thinner every year. Wages go up, fuel goes up, and the big retail customers push prices down.

units.summary: Margins are described as thin and getting thinner, with fuel, wage settlements and price pressure from large customers identified as pressures.
units.quote: Kaisa described margins as "thin and getting thinner" - fuel, wage settlements and price pressure from large customers.

units.summary: Several large retail contracts are due for renewal in 2027, and retail customers apply the strongest price pressure.
units.quote: Retail customers apply the strongest price pressure, and several large retail contracts are due for renewal in 2027.

units.summary: The company wants to grow without hiring more office staff for each new customer.
units.quote: We want to grow, but we cannot keep hiring more office people for every new customer.

units.summary: The strategy sets a goal to reduce manual office work by 30% by 2028.
units.quote: In our new strategy we have a goal to reduce manual office work by 30% by 2028.

units.summary: The strategy aims to reduce manual work in office processes by 30% by the end of 2028, so growth does not require additional office staff.
units.quote:
reduce manual work in office processes by 30 % by the end of 2028
so that growth does not require additional office staff.

conflicts.description: The recording and meeting notes estimate around/about 130 employees, with agency staff additional; the company overview gives 134 people measured as full-time equivalents at the end of 2025. The discrepancy is unresolved because no source hierarchy determines which figure to follow, and the sources describe the measure differently.
